Hi Rishi,

As we start planning our renewal (term ends 2027-06-30), the finance and platform teams want to align the contract with our fiscal year and our expected capacity increase. A few asks from our side:

- Can Redwood provide a structured pricing ladder that maps commit tiers to per-token pricing for multi-year commits? We want to see sample ramps (12/24/36 months) that include an annualization schedule.
- We'd like to co-term with our fiscal year (target co-term 2028-01-01) if possible — is pro-rated alignment supported?
- Procurement needs a draft amendment for internal review and a DocuSign-ready version once we agree on terms.

Attached: Nimbus_Proposed_Ramp_Schedule.xlsx (expected usage by quarter).

Primary goals: predictable unit economics as we scale, and a path for capacity increases over year 1 without frequent renegotiation.

Can we set a 30-minute sync early next week? 

Thanks,
Olivia Huang
Head of ML Platforms
Nimbus Health

Hi Olivia — thanks for the clear ask and the ramp spreadsheet. We can absolutely do a structured pricing ladder and support a co-term on your requested date. High-level options I suggest we review on a quick sync:

Option A — 3-year annualized commit (lowest unit price):
- Annual billing with decreasing per-token price each year as commit increases
- Best for predictable spend, but requires yearly commit guarantees

Option B — 2-year ramp with frontloaded credits (recommended for growth customers):
- Frontloaded credit in year 1 to offset ramp risk; ramp schedule ties monthly usage to committed buckets
- Mid-term re-evaluation window at month 9 for capacity top-ups

Option C — Co-term single-year with staged true-up:
- Align to fiscal co-term with pro-rata credit for partial first year
- Quarterly true-ups to avoid surprises

I've attached a draft pricing ladder and an amendment template (redwood_amendment_pricing_ladder_v3.pdf) that maps those options to sample numbers based on your ramp. Laura and Aditya — can you weigh in on acceptable billing cadence and which option preserves our margin while meeting their predictability ask?

Proposed next steps:
1) 30-min sync early Tue (May 4) to pick an option
2) Redwood to produce DocuSign-ready amendment once option chosen
3) Procurement to confirm billing preference (monthly vs annual)

Thanks — available Tue 9–11am PT.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Rishi / Laura — quick internal note before Tue's sync:

- Margin guardrails: for Option B we should target ~15–20% blended margin across year 1/2 to be comfortable; frontloaded credit can be structured as service credits, not cash back.
- Billing cadence: offer both annual and monthly invoicing with a modest premium (~3%) for monthly to cover billing overhead.
- True-up mechanics: set quarterly true-ups with a 30-day notice for capacity top-ups; if they top up >25% of committed tokens in a quarter, trigger a pricing re-eval.

I'll prepare a short one-pager that maps expected $/token at three commit breakpoints using Nimbus's spreadsheet. Rishi — if they want a DocuSign draft after Tue, I'll fast-track legal review.
